flagged.title: Electrolysis
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly affirms that aluminium rusts and refers to the oxide layer as 'aluminium's rust', directly contradicting the lesson text and teaching a misconception that loses marks under GCSE mark schemes where rusting applies strictly to iron.

mark_affecting.video_says: does aluminium rust? Well, surprisingly, yes! ... the absolutely crucial point to take away is that aluminium's rust is actually a protective superpower.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Additionally, there is a common misconception that aluminium 'rusts'. In fact, aluminium reacts quickly with oxygen in the air to form a thin, tightly bonded aluminium oxide layer. Unlike iron rust, this layer is impermeable and protective — it prevents any further oxidation.
